name: Plains Cree

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Plains Cree (plai1258).

notes: Research. Algonquian (Cree) variety of the Canadian plains written in the Standard Roman Orthography. Long vowels carry a circumflex (â ê î ô); c=[ts] (ranging to [tʃ]). Stops and s are underlyingly voiceless but voice intervocalically, which is left unencoded. Preaspiration and predictable allophony are not recovered from spelling, raising the PER floor. Grapheme table checked against Wolfart (1973, 1996): no discrepancy found. Stress is documented rather than encoded as a rule (see `stress.notes`): Wolfart's algorithm assigns stress differently by word length (final in disyllables, antepenultimate in longer words), which this project's single `default_position` cannot express in full; `default_position=-3` covers the common (3+ syllable) case and the 2-syllable exception is left as an honest documented gap rather than a wrong rule.

stress.notes: Wolfart (1996, Sketch of Cree) documents that Plains Cree stress is independent of vowel length: 2-syllable words stress the final syllable, while words of 3+ syllables stress the antepenultimate syllable. `default_position=-3` models the longer (and more frequent multi-morpheme) case; the disyllabic exception is not separately encoded (no field expresses a word-length-conditioned rule) and is documented here rather than silently wrong.
